title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation
abstract: arXiv:2611.18346v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accessible mobility is user-conditioned rather than scene-intrinsic, as walkable paths for one embodiment are inaccessible to another. Yet, existing benchmarks evaluate traversability under a fixed and limited embodiment. We present Vision-Language Accessible Navigation (VLAN), containing 1,000 scenes, 20K navigation trajectories, and 160K keyframes across diverse lighting, environmental conditions, scene semantics, and path geometries. For each trajectory, VLAN provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility features for legged and wheeled agents, including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments, while everyday obstacles and accessibility labels are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk, and Blocked. translated_abstract: 无障碍通行取决于用户而非场景本身，因为一种身体形态可以通行的路径，对另一种身体形态来说可能是无法通行的。然而，现有的基准测试仅在固定且有限的身体形态下评估可通行性。我们提出了视觉-语言无障碍导航，包含1,000个场景、2万条导航轨迹和16万关键帧，涵盖多样的光照、环境条件、场景语义和路径几何。对于每条轨迹，VLAN为腿式和轮式智能体（包括人形机器人、四足机器人以及有视觉或行动障碍的人士）提供特定于身体形态的动作和无障碍特征，同时将日常障碍物和无障碍标签归类为可通过、绕行、高风险和阻塞。与仅以目标为导向的评估不同，我们的基准通过到达目标、碰撞感知和无障碍对齐等指标来衡量物理安全性以及与用户特定约束的一致性。
tldr: 提出首个面向多种身体形态（人形/四足机器人及视觉或行动障碍人士）的大规模视觉-语言无障碍导航基准VLAN，通过无障碍对齐指标评估导航的物理安全性与用户特定约束的契合度。
en_tdlr: VLAN is a large-scale vision-language navigation benchmark that provides embodiment-specific actions and accessibility labels for diverse agents and impaired users, evaluating physical safety and user-specific accessibility constraints beyond goal-reaching metrics.
